narrative.summary: Barbados has no AI strategy, AI law or AI guidance. Its only AI-relevant national instrument is the Data Protection Act, 2019-29, in operation since 31 March 2021 (apart from its registration provisions), which gives people a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing and requires data protection impact assessments for automated profiling. The Act is supervised by the Data Protection Commission within the Ministry of Industry, Innovation, Science and Technology. A Centre for AI Innovation and Governance has been announced but no founding document is published.

instruments.current_status: Enacted with the Governor-General's assent on 12 August 2019 and published as a Supplement to Official Gazette No. 66 of 15 August 2019. By Proclamation (S.I. 2021 No. 24, Official Gazette of 26 March 2021) the Act came into operation on 31 March 2021, except sections 50, 51, 52, 55, 56 and 57, which were not brought into operation by that Proclamation.
instruments.summary: Barbados's GDPR-modelled data protection law regulating the collection, keeping, processing, use and dissemination of personal data by data controllers and processors, supervised by a Data Protection Commissioner. Section 18 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects (with contract, enactment and consent exceptions and required safeguards, and a stricter rule for sensitive data), and data subjects must be informed of the existence of automated decision-making and its logic. A data protection impact assessment is required for systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing, including profiling, on which significant decisions are based.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national legislation with explicit rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs AI systems that process personal data.

leads.title: Cybercrime Bill, 2024
leads.note: Bill (Objects and Reasons dated 2024-01-29) to repeal the Computer Misuse Act, Cap. 124B; referred to a Joint Select Committee in the Senate (barbadosparliament.com). The tabled text (https://www.barbadosparliament.com/uploads/bill_resolution/48c581fc50f5357214a37caab9189066.pdf) contains no explicit AI or deepfake provision; commentary says it would cover AI-generated child abuse material. Re-check only if an enacted version adds AI/synthetic-media provisions. 2026-10-18: Parliament gazette archive title search (2019-2026) for 'Cybercrime' returned no enacted Act; still a lead.
